items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names are clear (`final_key`, `rhs_json_path`), but nothing explains why the final key uses `json.dumps(str(final_key))` while earlier segments use compile_json_path. The template lines in as_sqlite are repeated in the new branch and the old fallback, which makes it harder to follow.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: No overridable hook or subclass. KeyTransformIsNull.as_sqlite/as_oracle rebuild the JSON_TYPE/JSON_EXISTS SQL by hand (copy-paste). The `isinstance(self.lhs, KeyTransform)` check is effectively always true, so the old HasKey fallback is dead code.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: No error-handling problems, but there is an edge-case regression: KeyTransformExact.as_oracle still calls `HasKey(self.lhs.lhs, self.lhs.key_name)`. With the new final-key quoting, `value__d__0=None` on Oracle treats 0 as an object key instead of an array index.

items.name: Array-index semantics kept for isnull / exact=None paths
items.name_zh: isnull / exact=None 路径保留数组下标语义
items.evidence: The has_key family is fixed in shared as_sql, so it applies to SQLite, MySQL and Oracle. The isnull paths keep array-index behaviour, but by duplicating SQL rather than using a subclass. KeyTransformExact.as_oracle (exact=None) was missed and still uses plain HasKey.
